item.title: Constant Approximation of Fr\'echet Distance in Near-Linear Time
item.description: arXiv:2611.00240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a deterministic algorithm that approximates the Fr\'echet distance between two polygonal curves in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $n$ and $m$ vertices within a constant factor in $O((m+n)^{1+\varepsilon})$ time, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and fixed dimension $d$. The approximation factor depends only on $\varepsilon$ and $d$. No assumption on the input curves is needed, and the algorithm also reports a matching certifying the approximation. The same result holds for the discrete Fr\'echet distance. Our result extends the line of work initiated by Cheng, Huang, and Zhang (2025), who gave the first constant-factor approximation in strongly subquadratic time, to near-linear time. For two $n$-vertex curves, the best previous running time was $\widetilde{O}(n^{5/3})$, due to van der Horst and Ophelders (2026). Our algorithm bootstraps between two primitives: a data structure that preprocesses a single curve for comparing any two of its subcurves, and a query procedure that compares subcurves of two different curves. Given the data structure for one curve, we compare it with another curve using a surrogate assembled from subcurves of the former. The surrogate is shared by all possible starting points of a matching. Conversely, faster queries make the next data structure cheaper to build. After a number of rounds that depends only on $\varepsilon$, both preprocessing and query time are $O((m+n)^{1+\varepsilon})$. To make each round's output reusable by the next, we compactly summarize how matchings can enter and leave a pair of subcurves. These summaries can be applied to different starting points and retain the information needed to report the matchings.
item.dc:creator: Haoqiang Huang, Zihe Wang, Shuo Zhang

item.title: Catenary Visibility: A Geometric Framework for Planning with Tethered Robots
item.description: arXiv:2611.00324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces \emph{catenary visibility}, a new geometric visibility concept for a robotic system consisting of a ground robot tethered to an aerial drone. The tether is modeled as an extensible catenary curve with bounded length, providing sustained power and significantly extending operational range. We define a point on the ground plane as \emph{catenary-visible} from a target point in 3D if there exists a collision-free catenary connecting them, given a set of obstacles. This paper introduces a geometric framework for visibility-aware planning of a tethered marsupial system, addressing the computational challenge of determining the feasible deployment locus: the collection of points in the ground plane that are catenary-visible from a given target in 3D space. We begin by solving the 2D subproblem, where the obstacles, target, and the ground vehicle's line of motion are all constrained to a single vertical plane. Our algorithm for this case computes the complete set of feasible launch points along the motion line and simultaneously determines the range of viable cable lengths for each. We also consider the query problem of finding all collision-free length ranges for a given location of the ground robot. Building upon this planar solution, we then generalize the approach to three dimensions, deriving a 3D solution for a constrained class of obstacles.
item.dc:creator: B. \'Abrego, J. M. D\'iaz-B\'a\~nez, S. Fern\'andez, D. Flores-Pe\~naloza, V. S\'anchez-Canales

item.title: Hamiltonian Cycle Construction in Rectangular Grid Graphs with Three-Stacked Triangular Holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.00364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hamiltonian cycle problem is NP-complete for general grid graphs, while several structured classes admit efficient construction algorithms. In this paper, we investigate Hamiltonian cycle construction in rectangular grid graphs containing a three-stacked right-triangular hole. We explore two complementary approaches based on the geometric structure of the hole and the parity properties of rectangular subgraphs. The first approach constructs a Hamiltonian path in the complementary reversed staircase region, extends it into an inner Hamiltonian cycle, and merges it with a cycle in the surrounding graph. The second approach partitions the graph into six rectangular subgraphs and constructs a global Hamiltonian cycle by merging local cycles along compatible boundaries. When odd-sized rectangular subgraphs prevent direct cycle construction, we develop parity-based repartitioning techniques that transform selected configurations into even-sized rectangles. We provide constructions for adjacent and nonadjacent odd-sized configurations and investigate reductions for cases involving multiple odd-sized regions. These results establish a constructive framework for Hamiltonian cycles in grid graphs with staircase-shaped holes and identify the remaining cases requiring further analysis.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Chen, Dianna Xu

item.title: Representation-Aware Closed-Surface Parameterization: Exact Sensitivity Analysis and Pole-Aware Planar Preconditioning
item.description: arXiv:2611.00721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface parameterization is a fundamental task in geometry processing and shape analysis. For topologically closed surfaces, it is common to parameterize them onto a standardized closed domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a prime example being a unit sphere for genus-0 closed surfaces. Many mapping methods use planar projections and perform computations on the plane rather than directly on the 3D surface. However, perturbations introduced before projection or geometric evolution propagate through the computation and may affect map quality, convergence, stopping behavior, and geometric validity. In this work, we formulate representation sensitivity as a branchwise input--output problem, separating smooth propagation through active Jacobians from changes in anchors, stopping rules, and fallback events. Under consistent piecewise-linear assembly, the unmodified south-pole Beltrami correction in the FLASH method for spherical conformal parameterization reduces exactly to source-mesh harmonic extension. On a fixed-anchor branch, the corrected map factors into chart transition, harmonic propagation, and inverse stereographic projection, yielding an explicit sensitivity Jacobian and a finite-triangle conditioning bound. Separately, we introduce a bounded five-parameter affine preconditioner over planar scale, translation, and anisotropy and evaluate candidates on the corrected spherical map. Across 30 genus-0 surfaces, it reduces median polar upper-tail log-condition and chord-angle distortion by $10.17\%$ and $10.97\%$, respectively, with both measures improving on every mesh. We also apply the framework to other spherical mapping methods including the conformalized mean-curvature flow and spherical density-equalizing maps. Altogether, our work highlights the importance of representation selection as a structural and practical component of spherical parameterization and downstream computation.
item.dc:creator: Zixi Yi, Gary P. T. Choi

item.title: From Static Models to Editable CAD: A Design-Intent-Aware Framework for Reverse Parametrization
item.description: arXiv:2611.00777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neutral CAD formats such as STEP typically preserve geometry but not feature histories or parameter dependencies. Thus, they are inherently limited for iterative design that requires modifications, a critical limitation for design optimization that relies on iterative processes. This study presents a design-intent-aware reverse-parametrization framework that converts history-free STEP parts into editable Grasshopper definitions and represents their assembly relations. Without task-specific training, the framework combines kernel-measured features, geometric relations, a compressed attributed adjacency graph, and multiview renderings. An LLM assigns dimensions independent, fixed, or dependent roles, confirms candidate joints, and interprets verification reports. Kernel- and rule-based modules perform measurement, parameter binding, geometry construction, and verification. Evaluation distinguishes default-shape preservation, design-intent reflection, and edit validity, with the latter examined through assembly-level editing examples involving checks for geometry regeneration, joint alignment, interference, and mechanism closure. As an example, five components of a mechanical mechanism were used, and across 25 runs, the mean global and analytic-feature-region intersection over unions (IoUs) were 0.984 and 0.983, respectively; all runs passed the combined shape-preservation criterion. In a separate request experiment, the requested dimension was selected as an independent variable in 19 of 20 runs. Product-level examples show coordinated changes in part geometry and assembly design while preserving assembly relations and avoiding inter-part interference. These results demonstrate editable reconstruction of history-free CAD models under the evaluated geometric and assembly constraints, indicating potential for subsequent design optimization.
item.dc:creator: Yurim Lee, Sumin Lee, Namwoo Kang

item.title: Quadratic Reconfiguration of Plane Spanning Paths on Two-Layer Point Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.03299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider a crossing-free polygonal path with $n$ vertices and a flip operation that removes an edge and adds another one, without changing the vertex set and keeping the path crossing free. It is conjectured that any two such paths can be transformed into each other by a sequence of flips. Recently, Kleist et al. (2024) proved the conjecture for the special cases of vertices arranged in two convex layers. However, the number of flips in their proof may be exponential. In this paper, we show that $O(n^2)$ flips suffice. More precisely, for a two-layer point set $S=L_0\cup L_1$, where $L_0$ and $L_1$ denote the outer and inner layers, respectively, our method uses $O(|L_0|+|L_1|^2)$ flips.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Avril, Yan Gerard, Guilherme D. da Fonseca

item.title: CuPH: Parallel Cubical Persistent Homology via Level-Synchronous Component Tracking
item.description: arXiv:2611.01078v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Persistent homology (PH) is a mathematically principled multi-scale topological descriptor of shape and connectivity in data. It is widely applied in image classification, segmentation, and shape analysis across medical and aerial imaging, providing structural information that pixel-wise deep learning may overlook. Standard cubical PH decomposes an image into cubical cells (vertices, edges, and squares) and reduces them sequentially in filtration order. This sequential reduction has $\Theta(n)$ parallel depth for an $n$-pixel image, limiting within-image GPU parallelism and constraining its use in topology-aware deep learning. We introduce CuPH, a GPU-based parallel algorithm for computing cubical PH on 2D images that operates directly on pixels rather than cubical cells. CuPH buckets pixels by filtration values, activates them with a level-synchronous sweep, and tracks connected components with a lock-free union-find method. We prove that CuPH produces persistence diagrams identical to standard cubical PH on integer inputs, with a stability bound for floating-point inputs. CuPH reduces parallel depth from $\Theta(n)$ to $O(L\log n)$ for an image with $L$ intensity levels. We implement the level sweep as a single CUDA kernel, eliminating cross-level kernel-launch overhead. Empirically, CuPH is $18.6$--$99.6\times$ faster than the existing GPU baseline (CMP). As a drop-in PH backend, CuPH accelerates topology-aware classification ($4.2$--$16.7\times$) and segmentation ($8.3$--$44\times$) while preserving accuracy. It also enables computing full-image PH losses on high-resolution images, improving segmentation Dice by $2.2$--$4.6$ points over patch-local PH baselines and accelerating training by $25$--$31\times$.
item.dc:creator: Guangyu Meng, Pengfei Gu, Erin Wolf Chambers, Danny Z. Chen

item.title: An $\mathsf{FPRAS}$ for Mixed Volumes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) to estimate the mixed volume of $n$ arbitrary compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ specified by weak membership oracles. This disproves a longstanding conjecture of Gurvits (2009). $\textbf{AI Disclosure}$ The main ideas were generated entirely by GPT 6 Astra. The purpose of this paper is to provide a human-written exposition of the algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu

item.title: Every $k$-Quasi-Planar Graph Has Linearly Many Edges
item.description: arXiv:2611.01509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every fixed integer $k\ge2$, we prove that every simple graph on $n$ vertices drawn in the plane with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges has at most $C_kn$ edges, where $C_k$ depends only on $k$. We allow any finite number of proper crossings between two edges, including edges with a common endpoint. For $n\ge3$, removing a small disk around each vertex turns the drawing into a family of arcs on a sphere with $n$ boundary circles. Each arc joins two different boundary circles, and different edges have different unordered pairs of endpoint circles. The arcs are therefore essential and pairwise nonhomotopic, with endpoints allowed to move along their boundary circles during a homotopy. Any family of pairwise intersecting lifts to the universal cover projects to distinct graph edges that cross pairwise. Its size is consequently at most $k-1$. Beeker and Lazarovich's theorem on surface patterns then bounds the number of arcs. Their estimate is linear in the size of a triangulation, and an explicit triangulation of the $n$-holed sphere has linearly many edges and triangles.
item.dc:creator: Ankan Sadhu

item.title: Graphs Have Structure: Declarative Manifolds, 3D Z-Order Monoid Roll-ups, and Zero-Simulation Visual Analytics in a Graph DBMS
item.description: arXiv:2611.01879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every real-world graph is embedded in an ambient structural manifold: proteins fold in Euclidean space ($R^3$), telecom networks sit on a planetary surface ($S^2 \times R$), and ontologies and calendars form discrete subsumption posets ($(V, \sqsubseteq)$). Yet property graph databases treat node coordinates as opaque payload scalars, leave spatial proximity edges unindexed, and force visualizers into $O(V^2)$ client-side force-directed simulations that destroy true geometry and truncate hierarchy roll-ups. We elevate ambient manifold structure to a first-class primitive in Samyama Graph. First, we introduce a declarative and auto-detected structural convention contract (samyama.structure/1) persisted in .sgsnap headers that binds node labels to Euclidean 3D, Geo-Spherical, Causal Spacetime, or Poset Hierarchy manifolds. Second, we show that both discrete posets (via Order-Embedded Hierarchy $[tin, tout]$ DFS intervals) and continuous 3D manifolds (via a 63-bit 3D Morton Z-order Structural-Geometric Index, SGI) reduce regional aggregation to 1D rank-interval monoid folds answered directly from index-resident Fenwick trees (SUM, COUNT) and Segment Trees (MIN, MAX). At $100,000$ 3D nodes, SGI builds in $28.14$ ms and answers Morton-interval SUM and MAX roll-ups in $0.048\,\mu$s and $0.104\,\mu$s---$8,345.1\times$ and $3,824.4\times$ faster than property scans. Third, we introduce 3D voxel-hashed virtual contact edges weighted by Topological--Geometric Stress $\sigma(u,v) = d_{graph}(u,v) / d_{manifold}(u,v)$ to isolate long-range tertiary folds, plus manifold-guided $A^*$ shortest-path search that cuts explored states by up to $3.80\times$ over Dijkstra. Fourth, we replace client layout simulation with server-computed 3D Cone-Tree/Ribbon coordinates and a non-WebGL 2.5D Isometric projection with painter's-order depth sorting and sub-millisecond Level-of-Detail (LoD) macro-cuts.
item.dc:creator: Madhulatha Mandarapu, Sandeep Kunkunuru

item.title: On Guarding Line Arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2611.02046v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the problem of guarding a set of straight lines in the plane by selecting a minimum-cardinality set of points such that every line contains at least one selected point. This problem is known to be strongly NP-hard \cite{megiddo}. We investigate approximation algorithms for the problem and analyze their performance guarantees under various structural assumptions on the underlying line arrangement. In particular, we present approximation schemes based on set-cover techniques, relaxation methods, and properties of maximal lines. We establish constant-factor bounds on the approximation ratio for several classes of arrangements and derive relationships between the guarding number and the incidence parameters of the arrangement. Connections with Dirac-type incidence results are also explored.
item.dc:creator: Valentin Brimkov

item.title: Pair-Relative Partial Equivariance for Rotation-Robust Keypoint Descriptor Matching
item.description: arXiv:2611.02751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learned keypoint descriptors trained on upright imagery often fail under large in-plane rotation. Steerers address this by applying a single exact SO(2) representation to the descriptor space, but this global group constraint can be too rigid for keypoint descriptors, whose angular responses need not follow a single group representation. We propose pair-relative partial equivariance, which measures equivariance under the empirical distribution of relative rotations in image pairs, and PaSteer, a relaxed descriptor-steering framework that allows the steering map to leave the exact representation manifold while retaining the lightweight, backbone-free design of steering. PaSteer instantiates this relaxation with two variants: an identity-preserving residual steerer (PaSteer-soft) and a free-form Fourier steerer (PaSteer-free). We show that the per-angle optimal linear steerer for a fixed non-equivariant descriptor generally does not obey the group composition law, explaining why exact representations can be suboptimal in the frozen-descriptor regime. On Roto-360, MegaDepth-1500, AIMS, and IMC-PT, PaSteer consistently improves rotation-robust matching over an exact steerer on frozen DeDoDe descriptors, especially under large relative rotations, with minimal upright degradation.
item.dc:creator: Jongmin Lee

item.title: Non-simple Arrangements of Lines and Pseudolines with Many Triangles
item.description: arXiv:2611.03096v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study affine arrangements of an even number $n$ of lines and pseudolines with many triangles. For simple ones, Blanc's bound limits the number of triangular faces to $\lfloor n(n-5/2)/3\rfloor$. Adapting the Bartholdi-Blanc-Loisel doubling to the even case, we construct an infinite series of arrangements of $n=6\cdot2^t+2$ ($8,14,26,50,\ldots$) straight lines with two triple points and $(n(n-5/2)+1)/3$ triangles, one more than the simple bound allows. We obtain exhaustive enumerations of triangle-maximal pseudoline arrangements, simple or not, for even $n\le12$. For $n=6,8,10,12,14$ the maximum number of triangles, for both lines and pseudolines, is $7,15,25,38,54$; for $n=8,12,14$ every optimal arrangement has multiple points. All optimal arrangements for even $n\le12$ are realizable by straight lines, except two arrangements of 10 pseudolines, which are not stretchable. For the odd value $n=11$, no arrangement with $33$ triangles exists even with multiple points. We also obtain even arrangements by adding a line to odd ones. For $n\equiv2\pmod 6$ this again gives one triangle more than the simple bound, in pseudolines up to $n=44$ and in straight lines for $n=20$ and $n=32$. Doubling these pseudoline arrangements gives members of the series $18\cdot2^t+2$ and $30\cdot2^t+2$ with the same excess, up to $n=146$ and $n=242$, respectively; those with $n=38$ and $n=74$ are realizable by straight lines. These results lead us to conjecture that an arrangement of an even number $n$ of pseudolines has at most $\lfloor n(n-2)/3\rfloor-\lfloor n/6\rfloor$ triangles.
item.dc:creator: Roman Parpalak, Denis Utkin

item.title: Coresets for Continuous $k$-Center in Hyperbolic Space
item.description: arXiv:2606.16061v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study coresets for the continuous $k$-center problem in fixed-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^D$, where centers may lie anywhere in the space. For an input set $P$ of $n$ points, we construct an unweighted coreset of size $(k/\varepsilon)^{O(kD)}$ in $O(nkD(k/\varepsilon)^{O(kD)})$ time, independent of the enclosing radius. Every exact optimal solution for the coreset is a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation for $P$. The same construction also yields a strong coreset after adjusting the accuracy parameter. Our method combines local Euclidean grids at bounded scales with radial shells at larger scales. Hyperbolic balls induce spherical caps on representative spheres, whose multiplicative enlargement can be controlled by additive hyperbolic distance errors. A recursive ball-coverage certificate then selects a radius-independent set of input witnesses. We establish lower bounds of $\Omega_D(k\varepsilon^{-D})$ for $k\ge 8D$ and sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, and $2^{\Omega(k)}$ for $D\ge2$ when $\varepsilon=\Theta(1/k)$, ruling out bounds polynomial jointly in $k$ and $1/\varepsilon$. For $k$ sufficiently separated clusters, we obtain simultaneous additive and multiplicative weak coreset guarantees, with optimal worst-case size $\Theta_D(k\varepsilon^{-(D-1)/2})$ when both errors equal $\varepsilon$. In contrast, even under the same separation condition, no radius-independent additive weak coreset bound exists in the Euclidean plane for $k=2$.
item.dc:creator: Eunku Park

item.title: One Shot, Twenty-One Balls: A Computer-Assisted Proof of a Single-Stroke Total Clearance in an Idealized Model of Snooker
item.description: arXiv:2607.12995v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Snooker folklore holds that no single stroke can pocket all twenty-one object balls. We examine the claim in an explicit model: twenty-two equal disks on a rectangle with six pocket points, under constant rolling deceleration, frictionless collisions with normal restitution, and lossy specular cushions. We exhibit a configuration and a stroke, and prove in interval arithmetic that every stroke in an explicit box around it pockets all twenty-one object balls, so the set of successful strokes has positive measure. That set is a ribbon: every speed from 9.3213 to 12 m/s works, while the certified window of directions is 9.4813e-43 radians wide, a number explained by a first-order analysis of twenty near-grazing collisions. A second configuration, a near-frozen cluster, has a certified window 9.4e-4 radians wide, thirty-nine orders of magnitude wider; its certificate uses Taylor models of degree six. The strokes with a given list of events form a semialgebraic set, and the endpoints of the windows are algebraic numbers. For the regulation opening position we state the corresponding conjecture, and show that if it holds with a regular witness then a finite certified search establishes it.
item.dc:creator: Avner Kantor

item.title: The Rhythm of the Tiles: Narrow and Low Temperature Computation and Simulation in Synchronous Tile Self-Assembly
item.description: arXiv:2610.17112v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove that the synchronicity provided by the syncTAM can be leveraged to perform two additional feats impossible in the asynchronous aTAM. The aTAM has long been known to be equivalent to finite automata in the one-dimensional case. For our first set of results, we prove that this still holds when a finite, fixed amount of space is available in the second dimension. Yet, surprisingly, in the synchronous setting, a small, fixed, width is enough to simulate a Turing Machine. This holds even in the non-cooperative setting. For our second set of main results we prove that there exists a single set of syncTAM tiles that can be used to simulate any syncTAM system simply by using those tiles to create a scaled version of the seed structure of the original system and then letting the tiles from that set self-assemble from the scaled seed structure. While it has been shown (FOCS 2012) that such a tile set also exists in the aTAM for simulating all aTAM systems, that "intrinsically universal" (IU) tile set requires cooperativity (and is impossible without cooperativity as shown in SODA 2014). We prove there exists an IU tile set in the syncTAM that works without cooperativity. Furthermore, there exists a tile set that is IU for the class of directed systems (i.e. systems which each have a single terminal assembly) while remaining directed during simulation. This was shown to be impossible in the aTAM (FOCS 2016).
item.dc:creator: Florent Becker, Phillip Drake, Benjamin Durbin, Nicolas Ollinger, Brent Orlina, Matthew J. Patitz

item.title: Strong Lower Bounds for Weak Epsilon-Nets
item.description: arXiv:2610.40982v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P$ be a finite point set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. A weak $\varepsilon$-net for $P$ with respect to convex sets is a finite set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ intersecting every convex set containing at least $\varepsilon|P|$ points of $P$. Determining their optimal worst-case size was described by Alon, Kalai, Matousek, and Meshulam [Adv. Appl. Math., 2002] as "one of the truly important open problems in combinatorial geometry." We give elementary constructions which establish the first polynomially superlinear lower bounds in fixed dimension. Already in $\mathbb{R}^3$, we construct point sets for which every weak $\varepsilon$-net has size $\Omega(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$. More generally, for every fixed $d\ge3$, we obtain a lower bound of $\Omega_d(\varepsilon^{-\gamma_d})$, where $\gamma_d=\sqrt{d/2}+O(1)$. Consequently, no upper bound of the form $O_d(\varepsilon^{-C})$ can hold with an absolute constant $C$ which is independent of the dimension. Despite the recent progress on upper bounds, the strongest previous general lower bound remained $\Omega_d(\varepsilon^{-1}\log^{d-1}(1/\varepsilon))$, due to Bukh, Matousek, and Nivasch [Israel J. Math., 2011]. To obtain our results, we apply a quadratic lift to grid-based configurations with many point-line incidences. The bounds also yield polynomial separations between fractional and integral piercing numbers of convex families, and lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers.
item.dc:creator: Sujoy Bhore, Reilly Browne, Da Wei Zheng
